To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1), the ultrastructural cryoinjuries of mitochondria are correlated with their respiratory function.

the ultrastructural cryoinjuries of mitochondria are correlated with aspects of their functional integrity, as measured by oxygen consumption, respiratory control ratio, and cytochrome c oxidase activity, and that the correlation of structure with function is greater for mitochondria in slices frozen and thawed rapidly and slowly than in slices frozen and thawn slowly and rapidly, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between ultrastructural damage and respiratory function in cryoinjury of kidney mitochondria.
the effects of cryoinjury on mitochondria in terms of their ultrastructure and functional integrity.
the relationship between structure and function of mitochondria in tissue cells as affected by cryoinjury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ultrastructural cryoinjuries of mitochondria correlate well with their respiratory function, but not as well with their cytochrome oxidases.
the ultrastructural and functional changes of mitochondria in renal cortex slices after cryoinjury are correlated, and the correlation is fairly well defined.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ultrastructural damage to mitochondria correlated well with functional damage to mitochondria as well as with functional injury to extramitoehondrial factors in respi- ration.
ultrastructural damage to mitochondria is a good indicator for their loss of function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ultrastructural and functional changes in mitochondria are correlated and can be used in a predictive way to determine the degree of damage to mitochondria and to the respiratory chain.
ultrastructural evaluation of cryoinjury can be correlated with functional evaluation, and that the latter is a better indicator of damage to mitochondria than the former.
the correlation of structure-function in mitochondria is useful in evaluating the extent of injury in cryoinjury of tissue.
